question_text:
Maya used to revise only the night before a test. This term, she began studying for twenty minutes each evening. She says she now feels calmer before exams and remembers more afterwards.

What changed in Maya's study routine?

options.A: She studies in shorter regular sessions
options.C: She studies only in the morning
options.D: She studies with a private teacher

explanation: The passage says she now studies for twenty minutes each evening.

question_text:
A small café near the station removed half of its indoor tables and added a covered outdoor area. The owner says customers stay longer there during warm months, while the indoor space feels less crowded.

Why did the café change its seating?

options.B: To create a more comfortable use of space
options.C: To reduce the number of customers
options.D: To turn the café into a shop

explanation: The change made indoor seating less crowded and added useful outdoor space.

question_text:
Leo bought a second-hand laptop because a new model was outside his budget. Before paying, he checked the battery, keyboard and screen and asked for a short warranty from the shop.

What does the passage suggest about Leo?

options.B: He wanted the most expensive model
options.D: He borrowed the laptop from a friend

explanation: He checked key parts and asked for a warranty before buying.

question_text:
The town's new bus app shows live arrival times. It does not sell tickets yet, but passengers can save favourite stops and receive service alerts.

Which feature is NOT available in the app?
explanation: The text explicitly says the app does not sell tickets yet.

question_text:
Nina joined a school debate club mainly to become more confident speaking in front of others. After two months, she noticed another benefit: she had become better at listening carefully before replying.

What unexpected benefit did Nina notice?

options.A: She learned to listen more carefully

explanation: Listening carefully is described as an additional benefit.

question_text:
A community garden gives local residents small plots to grow vegetables. Members share tools and water, but each person is responsible for looking after their own plot.

What are members expected to do individually?

options.B: Look after their own growing area

explanation: Each member is responsible for their own plot.

question_text:
When a software company introduced one meeting-free afternoon each week, managers worried communication would suffer. Instead, employees reported finishing more focused work, while teams moved routine updates to short written messages.

What was the result of the change?

options.C: Focused work increased without stopping communication

explanation: The company preserved communication while increasing focused work.

question_text:
The science centre's new exhibition is designed for visitors to touch, test and move many of the displays. Staff say the goal is to make difficult ideas easier to understand through direct experience.

What is special about the exhibition?
explanation: Visitors are encouraged to interact directly with the displays.

question_text:
Oleh cycles to college when the weather is dry, but on rainy days he takes the metro. He says cycling is usually faster during morning traffic and also gives him some exercise.

Why does Oleh often choose to cycle?

options.A: It can save time and provides exercise
options.D: His college is outside the city

explanation: He mentions both speed in traffic and exercise.

question_text:
A bookshop began placing short staff recommendations beside selected novels. Sales of those books increased, especially when the notes explained who might enjoy the story rather than simply saying it was good.

Which recommendations were most effective?

options.B: Those describing the type of reader who might enjoy the book
options.D: Those written by customers who had not read the book

explanation: The passage says recommendations worked best when they explained who would enjoy the story.

question_text:
Researchers asked two groups of students to learn the same list of words. One group reread the list several times; the other repeatedly tried to recall the words without looking. A week later, the recall group remembered more.

What conclusion best matches the study?

options.B: Reading once always guarantees long-term memory
options.C: Trying to retrieve information can strengthen memory
options.D: Learning vocabulary is impossible without a teacher

explanation: The group practising recall remembered more after a week.

question_text:
The local pool now opens at 6:30 on weekdays. The earlier time was introduced after many residents said they wanted to swim before work or school.

Why was the opening time changed?

options.A: To close the pool during weekends
options.B: To reduce the number of swimmers
options.D: To meet demand for early swimming

explanation: Residents requested an earlier time before work or school.

question_text:
Sara planned to buy a printed travel guide but finally downloaded an offline city map instead. She knew mobile internet might be expensive abroad and wanted directions that would work without a connection.

Why did Sara choose an offline map?

options.C: It is always more detailed than every guide

explanation: Her main concern was using directions without internet access.

question_text:
A school replaced some traditional homework with short projects in which students choose examples from everyday life. Teachers found that students asked more questions in class because they wanted to check whether their examples really fit the topic.

How did the projects affect students?

options.A: They eliminated the need for lessons
options.C: They made students avoid real-life examples
options.D: They reduced all homework to zero

explanation: Students asked more questions to verify their examples.

question_text:
A small clothing brand started publishing repair guides for its jackets. At first this seemed likely to reduce sales, but the company says customers became more loyal because they trusted a brand that helped products last longer.

Why did the repair guides help the company?

options.B: They forced customers to buy new jackets immediately
options.C: They increased customer trust and loyalty
options.D: They removed the need for customer service

explanation: Helping products last longer strengthened trust and loyalty.

question_text:
The university café offers a discount to customers who bring a reusable cup. The programme aims to reduce the number of disposable cups used each day.

What is the purpose of the discount?

options.B: To increase the price of coffee

explanation: The discount encourages reusable cups and therefore less waste.

question_text:
After moving into a noisy street, Daniel first tried studying with music. He soon found that quiet background noise through headphones worked better because songs distracted him from reading.

Why did Daniel stop using music while studying?

options.C: He no longer needed to study

explanation: The passage says songs distracted him from reading.

question_text:
A local history project asked older residents to record memories of the neighbourhood. Students then compared these stories with old photographs and maps. The aim was not to prove every memory exact, but to understand how people experienced changes in the area.

What was the main goal of the project?

options.A: To prove every memory was perfectly accurate
options.B: To explore personal experiences of local change

explanation: The project focused on how residents experienced changes.

question_text:
An online course allows students to watch recorded lessons at any time, but live workshops are held twice a month. The workshops are used mainly for questions, discussion and practical tasks.

What are the live workshops mainly for?

options.B: Watching the same recorded lesson silently

explanation: Questions, discussion and practical tasks are interactive activities.

question_text:
The city planted young trees along several busy roads. Officials do not expect an immediate change in summer temperatures, but they hope the trees will provide more shade as they grow.

Why will the full benefit take time?

options.A: The city plans to remove the trees soon
options.D: The trees need time to grow

explanation: Young trees need to mature before they provide substantial shade.

question_text: I used to keep all my school deadlines in my head. _____ Now I check it every evening and rarely forget an assignment.

options.A: Then I started using a simple calendar app.
options.C: For example, calendars are always expensive.
options.D: As a result, I never write anything down.

explanation: The next sentence refers to checking 'it', so a calendar app fits logically.

question_text: The park was once almost empty in the evenings. The city added better lighting and repaired the paths. _____ Families and runners now use it much more often after work.

options.A: In contrast, the park was moved to another city.
options.B: As a result, people began to feel safer there.
options.C: Nevertheless, the paths were removed again immediately.
options.D: For this reason, nobody can enter the park.

explanation: Improved lighting and paths logically lead to greater safety and more use.

question_text: Online lessons can be convenient because students can learn from home. _____ Without a routine, it is easy to postpone work until later.

options.A: For example, internet access is never necessary.
options.B: Therefore, every online lesson is easier than school.
options.D: Similarly, students cannot choose when to study.

explanation: The contrast is convenience versus the need for self-discipline.

question_text: Lena wanted to read more books this year. She decided not to set an enormous target. _____ After a few months, reading had become part of her normal routine.

options.A: For example, she bought a television.
options.B: As a result, she gave away every book she owned.
options.C: However, she stopped reading on the first day.
options.D: Instead, she began with ten pages a day.

explanation: A small daily target explains how reading became a routine.

question_text: The school café introduced a reusable cup discount. At first, only a few students brought their own cups. _____ By the end of the term, the number had increased significantly.

options.A: Teachers then reminded students about the programme.
options.B: The café then banned all drinks.
options.C: No one was allowed to enter the building.
options.D: The discount was removed before it began.

explanation: Reminders can logically explain the later increase in participation.

question_text: Mark was nervous before giving presentations. He began practising them aloud at home and recording himself. _____ This helped him notice where he spoke too quickly.

options.A: He deleted every presentation before speaking.
options.B: He listened to the recordings afterwards.
options.C: He decided never to practise again.
options.D: He turned off the microphone during class.

explanation: Listening to recordings explains how he noticed his speaking speed.

question_text: Many people assume creativity appears only when inspiration arrives. In reality, creative professionals often rely on routines. _____ Regular work creates more opportunities for useful ideas to appear.

options.A: They refuse to repeat any process.
options.B: They avoid working until the perfect idea arrives.
options.C: They set aside time to produce ideas even on ordinary days.
options.D: They believe schedules always destroy creativity.

explanation: A regular creative routine supports the final sentence.

question_text: The town wanted more people to cycle to the centre. It created protected bike lanes on several busy roads. _____ Surveys later showed that new cyclists felt more confident using those routes.

options.A: Cyclists were asked to use only pavements.
options.B: The roads were closed to bicycles.
options.D: The lanes separated cyclists from faster traffic.

explanation: Protected separation from traffic explains increased confidence.

question_text: I often forgot new vocabulary after learning it once. _____ Reviewing words at increasing intervals helped me remember them much longer.

options.C: Nevertheless, I threw away my notes.
options.D: For example, I avoided old words completely.

explanation: Spaced repetition is directly explained in the next sentence.

question_text: A local shop began offering online ordering for customers who were short on time. _____ Customers could then collect their purchases on the way home.

options.B: Orders were prepared before the customer arrived.
options.C: Customers had to wait longer than before by design.
options.D: The collection desk opened only once a year.

explanation: Prepared orders make convenient collection possible.

question_text: Students sometimes highlight almost every line of a textbook because everything seems important. _____ A better strategy is to identify the central idea first and mark only information that supports it.

options.A: This removes the need to understand the text.
options.C: This can make the highlighting less useful.

explanation: If everything is highlighted, the method loses its ability to show what matters.

question_text: The weather forecast predicted heavy rain during our trip. We did not cancel the walk. _____ In the end, we stayed dry enough to enjoy the day.

options.A: As a result, we forgot to check the weather.
options.B: Therefore, we left all rain protection at home.
options.C: However, we chose the longest exposed route possible.
options.D: Instead, we packed waterproof jackets and changed the route.

explanation: Preparing for rain explains why the walk still worked.

question_text: The library created a shelf called 'Staff Picks'. Each recommendation included two short sentences about the book. _____ Many visitors said the notes helped them choose faster.

options.A: The notes focused on what kind of reader might enjoy it.
options.B: The books were hidden from visitors.
options.D: The staff refused to describe any book.

explanation: Useful reader-focused notes logically help visitors choose.

question_text: Emma wanted to spend less time checking her phone while studying. She placed it in another room for thirty minutes at a time. _____ She found it easier to concentrate because notifications no longer interrupted her.

options.A: She kept every notification at maximum volume.
options.B: She checked messages during each break instead.
options.C: She opened social media on another device continuously.
options.D: She stopped taking any study breaks.

explanation: Checking messages during planned breaks supports fewer interruptions while studying.

question_text: A team kept making the same small mistakes during a project. Instead of blaming individuals, they held a short review after each stage. _____ Over time, repeated errors became less common.

options.A: They made the process more confusing on purpose.
options.B: They agreed never to discuss mistakes.
options.C: They recorded what went wrong and changed the process.
options.D: They removed all deadlines and responsibilities.

explanation: Identifying causes and changing the process explains fewer repeated errors.

question_text: The community centre offered a free trial week for its fitness classes. _____ Many participants later joined because they had discovered which class suited them best.

options.A: The centre closed during the trial week.
options.B: Everyone had to buy a yearly membership first.
options.D: People could try several different sessions before choosing.

explanation: Trying several classes explains better-informed membership choices.

question_text: We arrived at the station earlier than necessary. _____ We had enough time to find the correct platform and buy water before boarding.

options.A: That turned out to be useful.
options.B: As a result, we missed the train immediately.
options.C: However, the station did not exist.
options.D: Therefore, we went home without checking anything.

explanation: The next sentence lists benefits of arriving early.

question_text: The teacher stopped giving one long vocabulary test at the end of each month. Instead, she used short weekly quizzes. _____ Students also received feedback sooner and could review weak words before the next quiz.

options.A: This made vocabulary disappear from the course.
options.C: This prevented students from seeing their mistakes.
options.D: This meant students studied only once a month.

explanation: Frequent quizzes naturally encourage regular revision and faster feedback.

question_text: A company asked customers why they abandoned an online order. Many said the checkout required too many steps. _____ Completion rates improved soon after.

options.A: The company hid the final price until after payment.
options.B: The company added several extra pages to checkout.
options.C: The company simplified the form and removed unnecessary fields.
options.D: The company stopped listening to customer feedback.

explanation: Simplifying the checkout directly addresses the reported problem.

question_text: My first attempt at baking bread was disappointing because I cut it immediately after it came out of the oven. _____ The next loaf had a much better texture.

options.A: Then I placed the dough in the freezer before baking.
options.B: The second time, I used no flour at all.
options.C: After that, I stopped using an oven.
options.D: The second time, I let it cool before slicing it.

explanation: Letting bread cool before slicing explains the improved texture.

question_text: The new study room is usually quiet, so it is a good place to _____ on difficult homework.
explanation: The natural collocation is 'concentrate on' homework.

question_text: Please _____ attention to the instructions before you begin the task.
explanation: The fixed collocation is 'pay attention'.

question_text: The organisers had to _____ the outdoor event because of the storm.
explanation: An event can be cancelled because of bad weather.

question_text: I was tired, but a short walk helped me _____ my energy.
explanation: 'Regain energy' means get your energy back.

question_text: This app allows users to _____ their progress over several weeks.
explanation: 'Track progress' means monitor how it changes over time.

question_text: The teacher asked us to _____ an example from everyday life.
explanation: 'Provide an example' is the correct collocation.

question_text: The company decided to _____ feedback before changing the product.
explanation: Companies commonly 'gather feedback' from users.

question_text: It took me a few days to _____ used to the new timetable.
explanation: The expression is 'get used to'.

question_text: We were running _____ of time, so we skipped the final activity.
explanation: 'Run out of time' means have almost no time left.

question_text: The museum is within walking _____ of the station.
explanation: The fixed phrase is 'within walking distance'.

question_text: The article _____ an important point about how habits are formed.
explanation: We 'raise a point' or 'raise an issue' in discussion.

question_text: I did not recognise him at first because he had _____ his hairstyle completely.
explanation: 'Change your hairstyle' is the natural verb choice.

question_text: The course is designed to _____ students with practical interview skills.
explanation: 'Equip someone with skills' means give them the abilities they need.

question_text: The manager asked the team to _____ up with three possible solutions.
explanation: The phrasal verb is 'come up with' an idea or solution.

question_text: Make sure you _____ a copy of the file before editing it.
explanation: You save a copy of a digital file.

question_text: The train was delayed, but we still arrived in _____ for the meeting.
explanation: 'In time for' means early enough not to miss something.

question_text: Her explanation was clear and _____, so everyone understood the main idea quickly.
explanation: 'Concise' means brief but clear, fitting the context.

question_text: The website lets you _____ the results by price, date or rating.
explanation: Digital results can be filtered using criteria.

question_text: The project was more difficult than expected, but the team managed to _____ it through.
explanation: 'See something through' means continue until it is completed.

question_text: Regular practice can make a noticeable _____ to your confidence when speaking.
explanation: The fixed phrase is 'make a difference'.

question_text: I _____ this book last week and finished it yesterday.
explanation: A finished past time ('last week') requires Past Simple.

question_text: By the time we arrived, the film _____.
explanation: Past Perfect describes an action completed before another past action.

question_text: If it _____ tomorrow, we will move the event indoors.
explanation: First Conditional uses Present Simple in the if-clause.

question_text: If I _____ more free time, I would join the course.
explanation: Second Conditional uses Past Simple after 'if'.

question_text: If they had checked the address, they _____ the wrong building.
explanation: Third Conditional uses would have + past participle for the result.

question_text: You _____ wear a helmet on this construction site. It is compulsory.
explanation: 'Must' expresses a strong rule or obligation.

question_text: You _____ have called a taxi; the station is only five minutes away.
explanation: 'Needn't have' means the action was unnecessary, though it happened.

question_text: She is _____ engineer who works for a renewable-energy company.
explanation: 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article is 'an'.

question_text: This is the café _____ we first met.
explanation: 'Where' refers to the place in which something happened.

question_text: The new bridge _____ next year if the project stays on schedule.
explanation: Future passive is 'will be + past participle'.

question_text: He said that he _____ the report the following day.
explanation: In reported speech, future 'will' commonly shifts to 'would'.

question_text: I enjoy _____ new places on foot when I travel.
explanation: 'Enjoy' is followed by a gerund (-ing form).

question_text: We decided _____ the earlier train to avoid traffic.
explanation: 'Decide' is followed by the infinitive with 'to'.

question_text: Hardly _____ the presentation when the internet connection failed.
explanation: After 'Hardly' at the beginning, inversion is used: 'Hardly had we started...'

question_text: There are _____ students in the room today than yesterday.
explanation: 'Students' is countable, so the comparative is 'fewer'.

question_text: She has lived here _____ 2022.
explanation: 'Since' introduces the starting point of an action continuing to the present.

question_text: Neither Tom nor his friends _____ available this evening.
explanation: With 'neither...nor', agreement normally follows the nearer subject, 'friends'.

question_text: I wish I _____ so much time on my phone yesterday.
explanation: A regret about the past after 'wish' uses Past Perfect.

question_text: The task was _____ difficult that several students asked for extra time.
explanation: The structure is 'so + adjective + that'.

question_text: Not only _____ the answer, but she also explained why it was correct.
explanation: After initial 'Not only', subject–auxiliary inversion is required.
